topic: selective prediction; selective learning; adversarial sequence prediction
status: resolved literature-status correction based on one sampled 2019 paper and one full-text COLT 2021 follow-up; not a new open research lead
claim: The 2019 paper's open question about fitting a model to a selected future window has a later answer in the same selective-learning formulation: Qiao and Valiant's COLT 2021 hybrid exponential-weights learner achieves expected excess risk O((log log |L| + log log n)/log n), with an almost matching lower bound in key regimes. The class-size tradeoff changes under bounded recall, for which a nearly tight O(sqrt(log |L|/log n)) bound applies. This result should not be conflated with selective classification, where a model abstains on individual inputs.
positive_evidence: The 2019 full text defines selecting one future window and choosing a model to fit it, then explicitly asks whether its class-size dependence can improve.
The 2021 COLT full text states that Theorem 5 resolves the 2019 open problem and proves O((log log |L| + log log n)/log n) expected excess risk.
The 2021 paper gives an almost matching lower bound in the stated regimes and a separate nearly tight bound for bounded-recall learners, showing that the restriction changes the rate.
counterevidence: The guarantees concern a one-shot selected future window and an adversarial sequence fixed independently of the learner's prediction; they do not automatically transfer to standard online regret or abstention settings.
The lower bound is conditioned on non-adaptivity or sufficiently large model class, so it is not a universal matching lower bound for every selective learner and parameter regime.
This status correction is based on one follow-up paper, not an exhaustive search for later variants or practical deployments.

falsifiable_test: For any registry entry claiming the 2019 model-class question is still open, check whether its formal problem is exactly one selected future window, bounded losses, non-adaptive adversarial data sequence, and model-class excess risk. If so, compare its parameters against the COLT 2021 upper/lower bounds; retain an open label only for a materially different model (e.g. adaptive adversary, bounded memory, computational constraints, or repeated predictions). This is a literature-status adjudication, not a new experiment.
limitations: Two deeply checked primary sources resolve only the stated formulation. No systematic search for all subsequent extensions was made, and no empirical selective learner was implemented.

topic: birthday repetition; two-prover games; dense CSP hardness amplification
status: partial related-literature status update; exact general-game fixed-size question not established as resolved
claim: The 2016 paper leaves open value decay for low-value birthday-repeated games. A 2018 ECCC follow-up proves nontrivial value reduction and repeated decay for a refined birthday operator based on independent vertex inclusion, with projection-game and parameter restrictions. Because the operator differs from the original fixed-size subset game and the later theorem is scoped, the correct registry state is ‘related restricted variant established; exact original question unresolved/needs further source audit,’ not simply ‘open’ or ‘solved.’
positive_evidence: The sampled 2016 paper explicitly states that low-value birthday repetition is open and identifies additive-error barriers in its proof.
ECCC TR18-034 proves a refined birthday-repetition value bound and repeated-repetition decay for projection games under specified set-size/degree assumptions.
The ECCC report itself distinguishes the original uniform fixed-size subset operator from its refined independent-inclusion operator.
counterevidence: The 2018 result is a genuine amplification theorem and may suffice for some related applications, so the old direction cannot be described as wholly untouched.
The formal distribution and restrictions differ; this audit has not located an exact theorem matching the 2016 general-game, original-operator target.
This is not proof that no later exact resolution exists; the current-status literature search is targeted rather than exhaustive.

topic: stochastic k-TSP; adaptivity gaps; stochastic routing
status: bounded theory lead from one sampled full text and its primary conference record; novelty not established
claim: The O(1) adaptivity results for Stoch-Reward and Stoch-Cost k-TSP apply to independent per-vertex uncertainty and specific threshold/sum objectives; polynomial-time construction additionally assumes polynomial-size distribution supports. The same paper notes a superconstant adaptivity gap for the neighboring stochastic Orienteering problem. A precise next question is to characterize which dependence structures or objective changes first invalidate the constant gap, beginning with explicit pairwise/negative-dependence models and matched metrics.
positive_evidence: The full text defines Stoch-Reward k-TSP with independent, explicitly given discrete rewards and proves a non-adaptive O(1)-approximation; it provides a separate O(1) result for independent stochastic costs.
The paper states polynomial-time algorithms for polynomial-size distribution supports, distinguishing theorem existence from an unrestricted input-size implementation claim.
The ITCS paper record states that related stochastic Orienteering has a superconstant adaptivity gap, direct counterevidence to generalizing the k-TSP result across routing objectives.
counterevidence: A superconstant gap for stochastic Orienteering does not show that correlation breaks k-TSP; the objective, stopping rule, and feasible policies also differ.
The constant-gap theorem is already strong within its formal model, and the proposed dependence-structure extension may be known elsewhere; novelty is not established.
This audit does not construct correlated instances, prove a bound, or survey all stochastic-optimization variants.
